profiles.name: William Burke-White
profiles.bio: William Burke-White is a professor at the University of Pennsylvania Carey Law School and served on the U.S. Secretary of State’s Policy Planning Staff during the Obama administration. Educated at Harvard and Cambridge, he studies international law, institutions and foreign policy. His work connects legal analysis with decisions made in government and international affairs.

profiles.name: Jason Sello
profiles.bio: Jason Sello is a professor of pharmaceutical chemistry at the University of California, San Francisco, with doctoral training in biophysics at Harvard University. His research connects chemistry and biology to investigate antibiotics and bacterial systems. His background is relevant to students exploring how molecular research can address problems in human health.

profiles.name: Aziz Aboobaker
profiles.role: Professor of Comparative and Functional Genomics
profiles.bio: Aziz Aboobaker is a professor at the University of Oxford whose research investigates regeneration, stem cells and the evolution of animal biology. His laboratory uses organisms with remarkable regenerative abilities to understand how tissues are maintained and rebuilt. This work connects fundamental biological questions with modern genetics and genomics.

profiles.name: David McMillon
profiles.bio: David McMillon is an assistant professor at Emory University who earned his PhD in public policy at the University of Chicago and master’s degrees in mathematics and engineering at the University of Michigan. He studies education, intergenerational mobility and economic inequality, bringing quantitative tools to questions about opportunity and social outcomes.

profiles.name: Sebastian Rosato
profiles.bio: Sebastian Rosato is a professor of political science at the University of Notre Dame and coauthor, with John Mearsheimer, of How States Think. His background includes Harvard research fellowships, degrees from Cambridge, Oxford and the University of Chicago, and earlier work at Goldman Sachs. He studies foreign policy, great-power competition and international security.

profiles.name: Brian Stoltz
profiles.bio: Brian Stoltz is a professor of chemistry at Caltech and a recipient of Caltech’s Feynman Prize for Excellence in Teaching. His research in organic synthesis explores how chemists build complex molecules and develop new chemical reactions. His work brings together molecular design, experimental strategy and the chemistry underlying potential therapeutic compounds.

profiles.name: Samuel Kunes
profiles.role: Professor of Molecular and Cellular Biology
profiles.bio: Samuel Kunes is a professor of molecular and cellular biology at Harvard University. His research uses the fruit fly to investigate how nervous systems develop and how neural circuits support behavior and plasticity. His work connects genetics, cell biology and neuroscience through experimentally testable questions.

profiles.name: Anastasia Romanou
profiles.bio: Anastasia Romanou is a physical scientist at NASA’s Goddard Institute for Space Studies and has an adjunct appointment at Columbia University. Her research examines the global carbon cycle, ocean processes and climate change through Earth-system modeling. Her work connects mathematical models with questions about our planet’s future.

profiles.name: Achilles Venetoulias
profiles.bio: Achilles Venetoulias is an adjunct professor in finance at Columbia Business School. His background includes a Stanford PhD in statistics, teaching at MIT Sloan, and founding two hedge funds. He connects quantitative analysis with investment practice, including the use of mathematical models to understand financial risk and portfolio decisions.

profiles.name: Alexander Ploss
profiles.bio: Alexander Ploss is the Harry C. Wiess Professor in the Life Sciences at Princeton University. His scientific training includes Cornell and Memorial Sloan Kettering, followed by research at Rockefeller University. His laboratory investigates infectious diseases and develops experimental systems to understand how pathogens interact with their hosts.

profiles.name: Robin Murphy
profiles.bio: Robin Murphy is an experimental psychologist at the University of Oxford and a fellow of Corpus Christi College. His research investigates learning, reasoning and the processes underlying human behavior. His work offers a foundation for exploring psychological questions through careful experimental design and evidence.

profiles.name: Ronaldo I. Borja
profiles.role: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
profiles.bio: Ronaldo I. Borja is a professor of civil and environmental engineering at Stanford University and a recipient of the Maurice A. Biot Medal. His work in computational mechanics examines how materials and geological systems deform and fail. He is the author of Plasticity: Modeling & Computation, connecting mathematical theory with engineering simulation.

profiles.name: Philipp Koehn
profiles.bio: Philipp Koehn is a professor of computer science at Johns Hopkins University and a researcher in machine translation. He is known for contributions including the Europarl corpus and the Moses translation system. His work connects language, statistical modeling and artificial intelligence, with direct relevance to how computers learn to translate human language.

profiles.name: Peter Pietzuch
profiles.bio: Peter Pietzuch is a professor of distributed systems at Imperial College London and a co-director of its I-X initiative. His research explores the infrastructure behind cloud computing, secure systems and data-intensive applications. His work connects computer systems research with the practical challenges of making large-scale software reliable and efficient.

profiles.name: Haifeng Xu
profiles.role: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Data Science
profiles.bio: Haifeng Xu is an associate professor at the University of Chicago and directs the SIGMA lab. A former Harvard postdoctoral fellow and recipient of a Google Faculty Research Award, he studies multi-agent artificial intelligence, machine learning and computational economics. His work explores how algorithms make decisions and interact in markets and strategic environments.

profiles.name: Ryan Fang
profiles.bio: Ryan Yuhao Fang is an associate instructional professor in economics at the University of Chicago, where he also earned his PhD. His interests include microeconomic theory, information economics and behavioral decision-making. His work examines how people use information, respond to incentives and make choices under uncertainty.

profiles.name: Liam Francis Gearon
profiles.bio: Liam Francis Gearon is an associate professor of education at the University of Oxford and a senior research fellow at Harris Manchester College. His scholarship examines education, religion and politics, including the Oxford Handbook of Religion and Education. His work provides a foundation for research into how educational ideas and institutions shape public life.

profiles.name: Matthew Grimes
profiles.role: Professor of Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Futures
profiles.bio: Matthew Grimes is Professor of Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Futures at Cambridge Judge Business School. His research explores entrepreneurship, social innovation and how organizations respond to societal challenges. His work connects business strategy with questions about purpose, sustainability and the development of new ventures.

profiles.name: Steven Fischer
profiles.bio: Steven Fischer is an Emmy-nominated writer, producer and director. His creative background connects filmmaking with storytelling and visual communication. For students interested in film, his professional practice offers a reference point for examining how creative ideas are developed and communicated to an audience.

profiles.name: Thomas Meade
profiles.bio: Thomas Meade is the Eileen M. Foell Professor of Cancer Research at Northwestern University, with earlier research training at Harvard Medical School and Caltech. His work connects chemistry, molecular imaging and biosensors. He investigates tools that help researchers observe biological processes and explore new approaches to medical diagnosis.

profiles.name: Jan Van der Spiegel
profiles.bio: Jan Van der Spiegel’s career at the University of Pennsylvania includes serving as a professor of electrical and systems engineering and an associate dean. Penn recognized his student advising with the Ford Motor Company Award for Faculty Advising. His background brings together engineering scholarship, teaching and academic mentorship.

profiles.name: Jens Hagendorff
profiles.bio: Jens Hagendorff is a professor of finance at King’s College London. His experience includes work with the Bank of Spain and engagement with central banks, regulators and financial institutions. His research examines banking, corporate governance and risk, connecting financial evidence with decisions made by institutions and policymakers.

profiles.name: Jens Rittscher
profiles.bio: Jens Rittscher is a professor of engineering science at the University of Oxford, with earlier leadership experience in computer vision at GE Global Research. His work applies image analysis and machine learning to biomedical problems. His research connects advanced computing with the interpretation of complex biological and medical images.

profiles.name: Jiann-Wen Ju
profiles.role: Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
profiles.bio: Jiann-Wen Ju is a professor of civil and environmental engineering at UCLA and received a lifetime achievement medal for his contributions to damage mechanics. His research examines how materials behave, accumulate damage and fail. His work connects mathematical modeling with questions about structural performance and engineering reliability.

profiles.name: Helen Haste
profiles.bio: Helen Haste is a psychologist and education scholar who has held a visiting professorship at Harvard Graduate School of Education. Her work explores civic participation, moral development and young people’s engagement with society. She has also contributed to research for UNESCO’s Futures of Education initiative.

profiles.name: Gbenga Ibikunle
profiles.bio: Gbenga Ibikunle is a professor of finance at the University of Edinburgh Business School and directs its Centre for Financial Innovations. His work includes leadership in a research partnership supported by NatWest Group. He studies financial markets and innovation, connecting academic research with questions facing financial institutions.
